item.title: Motor vehicle tax in Zurich: calculation and payment
item.description: In the Canton of Zurich, the calculation, deadlines and payment of the motor vehicle tax follow cantonal rules; also check vehicle and address changes.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - It is a cantonal motor vehicle tax. - Calculation, deadlines and amounts follow cantonal rules. - Changes to the vehicle and address require official verification.
## Key facts - Subject → motor vehicle tax - Canton → Zurich - Administration → cantonal rules and offices - Verification → official source of the Canton - Tax system → federal, cantonal and municipal levels
In the Canton of Zurich, the motor vehicle tax must be treated as a cantonal matter. The topic includes calculation criteria, deadlines, payment and updates when the vehicle or address changes. The operational point is the road traffic office indicated by the Canton, together with the official source that makes it possible to verify requirements, deadlines and amounts.
### The jurisdiction not to be confused The first distinction concerns the tax level. The Swiss system comprises three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each Canton has its own law and its own multiplier; for municipalities, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax. This general framework does not replace the cantonal instructions on motor vehicle tax: for Zurich, it is necessary to follow the procedure dedicated to this tax.
Those who consult AFC/ESTV must remember that the authority deals with IFD and IVA. Motor vehicle tax instead falls under cantonal services: cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal taxes. dichiarazione delle imposte therefore remains a tool distinct from the instructions of the road traffic office of the Canton of Zurich.
Nor can social security or statistics acronyms resolve the calculation. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS, AI and LPP, and does not set taxes. UST/BFS produces statistics, not tax rates. The useful reference therefore remains the cantonal source, especially when the question concerns an amount, a deadline or an administrative update.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the consequence is practical: the name of the Canton indicates the level at which to look for the answer. The same verification is needed when switching to another vehicle or when the address changes. In both cases, the request must be referred back to the procedure of the competent office, without replacing it with general rules on IFD, IVA or social benefits. This separation prevents a cantonal item from being read as if it were set at national level. ## What changes in practice
The practical issue is not merely knowing that the tax is cantonal. It is understanding which event is changing the case: the ordinary calculation, the payment, the change of vehicle or the address. Separating these moments reduces the risk of using outdated information when a new verification is needed. The source places all the steps within the framework of cantonal rules and offices.
### Three situations to keep separate
| Situation | Check | Reference | |---|---|---| | Vehicle unchanged | criterion, deadline and payment | official source of the Canton | | Change of vehicle | whether the calculation, deadline or payment changes | road traffic office | | Change of address | updating procedure | competent office |
With the vehicle unchanged, the task is to follow the cantonal instructions and link the calculation to the deadline indicated for the case. There is no need to replace these instructions with a rule derived from another Canton. Cantonal services may have requirements, deadlines and amounts that must be verified with the competent authority.
A change of vehicle deserves a separate verification. It is not enough to assume that the previous payment also applies to the subsequent situation, or that the criterion used before remains identical. The correct question is whether the change affects the calculation, the deadline or the payment. The road traffic office and the official source of the Canton are the two references to compare.
Updating the address follows a different logic: it concerns the accuracy of the data with which the administration manages the case. Here too, it is advisable not to rely on generic instructions. The dedicated cantonal procedure must be followed, and it must be verified that the change has been taken into account for the updated case.
This distinction also helps in understanding the expense within the budget. Anyone comparing the motor vehicle tax with direct federal tax or VAT is comparing items governed by different authorities. For a broader view of everyday expenses, costo della vita in Svizzera can be used, while keeping the cantonal verification of the vehicle separate.
The criterion remains valid for those who move between Cantons: information found elsewhere does not replace that of the Canton of Zurich. The correct procedure arises from the intersection of the event, the competent office and the official instructions, not from an amount copied from a different case. ## How to proceed without confusing the offices
The procedure can be organized into five steps, all anchored in the Canton of Zurich. The objective is not to create an independent formula, but to reach the source or office that governs the specific case.
### Five operational steps
1. Classify the request. Establish whether you are looking for the calculation criterion, the deadline, the payment, the change of vehicle or the address update. 2. Start with the Canton. Look for the official source and the traffic office responsible for the matter, without using a page dedicated to IFD, VAT or social security as a reference. 3. Reconstruct the calculation. Read the criteria indicated for the case and use only the requirements and amounts reported in the cantonal instructions. 4. Check the deadline and payment. The deadline and the method of payment must be verified on the same official source; do not replace them with general dates or rules. 5. Update the record. If the vehicle or address changes, follow the step prescribed by the competent office and retain the reference used for the verification.
This outline separates the role of the cantonal administration from that of the federal bodies. AFC/ESTV is not the reference for this tax; UFAS/BSV concerns social security and UST/BFS statistics. The abbreviations help prevent sending the request to the wrong authority, but they do not replace verification of the traffic office.
If the vehicle does not change, the verification remains focused on the criteria, deadline and payment indicated for the Canton of Zurich. When a vehicle change occurs, however, it is necessary to check again whether the change affects the calculation or the deadline. Updating the address requires the same approach: follow the cantonal procedure and do not automatically apply instructions referring to another situation.
Financial planning must also keep the items separate. The motor vehicle tax is a cantonal charge; it must not be reconstructed through IFD, VAT or social security contributions. To estimate the overall budget related to working in Switzerland, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Social assistance in the Canton of Zurich: requirements and application
item.description: In the Canton of Zurich, the application starts from a condition of need: competent office, documents, benefits and cooperation obligations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Social assistance starts from a condition of need - Responsibility generally lies with Cantons and municipalities - The application requires documents and cooperation - Benefits, deadlines and amounts must be verified at cantonal level
## Key facts - Prerequisite: condition of need - Competent authority: municipal or cantonal office - Application: necessary documents - Procedure: cooperation obligations
In the Canton of Zurich, the application for social assistance starts from a condition of need. It is generally administered by the Cantons and municipalities according to need. The practical step indicated is to identify the competent municipal or cantonal office and follow the required procedure.
### Competence and content of the application
The process revolves around four elements: the situation of need, the application, the documents and the benefits. The competent office receives the request and verifies the necessary information according to the applicable rules. Cooperation is among the obligations associated with the procedure and must be maintained during the relationship with the authority.
| Element | Practical indication | |---|---| | Prerequisite | Condition of need | | Contact point | Competent municipal or cantonal office | | Application | Submission with the required documents | | Benefits | Rules and amounts to be verified at cantonal level | | Cooperation | Obligation in dealings with the office |
The concrete list of documents should not be replaced with an improvised standard list. Before submitting the application, it is advisable to ask the office which documentation accompanies the case and which steps follow. The same applies to requirements, deadlines and amounts: for cantonal benefits, the reference source is the Canton's official source.
### What not to confuse
Social assistance does not coincide with the tax process. The AFC/ESTV handles direct federal tax and VAT, while the cantonal administrations handle cantonal and municipal taxes. The UFAS/BSV also concerns social security, with AVS/AI/LPP, and does not set taxes. For the application in Zurich, the operational point of reference therefore remains the competent municipal or cantonal channel. This guidance avoids sending the request to an entity that performs another function and prepares the verification of the documents.
If health insurance appears among the items to clarify, the guide on cassa malati e LAMal helps keep premiums and assistance separate. ## The relationship with the family budget
A situation of need should not be assessed by isolating a single expense item. To find their bearings, those living in the canton of Zurich must separate social assistance from the other pillars that affect the budget and are handled by different offices. This distinction is also useful when preparing documentation, because an insurance premium, a social security contribution or a tax is not the same thing as a social assistance benefit.
### LAMal and premiums
LAMal/KVG is mandatory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival. It is private per-capita premium insurance: it is not a tax and it is not a wage contribution. Premiums vary by canton and region; premium reductions are a cantonal subsidy. In the budget accompanying an application, this item must be recognized for what it is, without automatically turning it into a social assistance benefit. For health insurance fund rules and premium reductions, the operational point of reference remains cantonal.
### Social security, taxes and cost of living
AVS/AHV, AI and LPP/BVG belong to social security. UFAS/BSV is the body indicated for this area, while social assistance is administered by cantons and municipalities according to need. This distinction helps avoid presenting the application as if it were a request for a pension or occupational pension.
Taxation also follows a different path: direct federal tax is added to cantonal and municipal taxes; each canton has its own law and multiplier, while the municipality applies the multiplier at the cantonal level. AFC/ESTV is responsible for direct federal tax and VAT. This information helps assess the cost of living without adding different items together under the same label.
In a hypothetical scenario, a person in a situation of need should first distinguish the items in their own budget, then separate LAMal/KVG premiums, social security and taxes, and finally ask the competent office which elements to document. Comparing with costo della vita in Svizzera can help organize the budget, but it does not replace the cantonal verification of the application and benefits. Amounts should not be inferred from generic examples either: the official source of the Canton remains the reference.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Preparing the application in the Canton of Zurich
The practical procedure can be organized into a simple sequence, without assigning an office responsibilities that belong to the cantonal or municipal level.
### Operational steps
1. Define the situation. Clearly describe the situation of need that motivates the application. The basis of social assistance is need; the application should therefore be linked to the situation for which support is requested.
2. Identify the contact point. Find the municipal or cantonal office responsible for your situation in the Canton of Zurich. Administration is generally cantonal and municipal: follow the channel indicated by the Canton or municipality.
3. Ask for the list of documents. Before submitting the application, ask which documents must accompany the request. The procedure requires documentation, but the specific list must be linked to the competent office and the applicable procedure. Avoid using generic templates as if they were valid for every case.
4. Check benefits and rules. Ask which benefits are provided, which requirements apply, which deadlines must be met and how the amounts are determined. For cantonal services, requirements, deadlines and amounts must be verified on the official source of the Canton.
5. Cooperate during the procedure. The duty to cooperate is part of the process. Maintain contact with the office and submit whatever is requested, without confusing this phase with a tax or social security application.
### Checks to keep separate
LAMal/KVG remains compulsory health insurance for residents, with per-capita premiums and premium reductions under cantonal responsibility. AVS/AHV, AI and LPP/BVG, on the other hand, belong to social security. If one of the two areas comes up during preparation, it must be handled through the relevant channel and not automatically incorporated into the assistance application.
The same criterion applies to direct federal tax and VAT, which fall under AFC/ESTV, while cantonal and municipal taxes are handled by the cantonal administrations. Keeping the files separate reduces the risk of contacting the wrong office and makes the application easier to understand.
After collecting the information from the Zurich office and completing the requested documents, you can check the effect of disposable income with the calcolatore stipendio, as the final practical step for organizing the budget.

item.title: Minimum wage in the Canton of Zurich: requirements and application
item.description: There is no federal minimum wage in Switzerland: in Zurich, cantonal regulations, collective agreements, checks and areas of responsibility must be verified.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal level → no federal minimum wage - Cantons → some have their own minimum wage - Alternative → collective agreements where there is no cantonal minimum wage - Verification → requirements, terms and amounts in the cantonal source
## Key facts - National rule → no federal minimum wage - Jurisdiction → potentially cantonal regulation - Contractual reference → collective agreements - Checks → the competent cantonal office
Switzerland does not have a federal minimum wage. Some cantons have their own, and this distinction is the first step for anyone who needs to assess an employment relationship in the Canton of Zurich.
For the search for Zurich canton minimum wage requirements and application, the point is therefore not to start from a national figure. It is necessary to establish whether cantonal regulation applies, which sectors it covers, what requirements it sets out and how checks are organized. The competent office must also be identified at the cantonal level.
### The scope of the rule
A cantonal minimum wage, where provided for, is not the same as a level applicable throughout Switzerland. The federal rule does not offer a single threshold; it leaves room for regulations by individual cantons. For this reason, in an assessment concerning Zurich, the official cantonal text must be the starting point before using the word minimum to describe the wage.
The review follows a concrete sequence: the scope of the regulation, any sectors concerned, application requirements, monitoring procedures and the competent office to use as a reference. These elements matter more than the mere geographical location of the workplace. An amount taken from another canton does not prove that the same rule applies in Zurich.
When there is no cantonal minimum wage, the source highlights the difference from collective agreements. The collective agreement is then the reference to examine for the employment relationship in question, without turning it into a federal minimum wage.
For a worker moving between cantons, the question cannot be resolved solely by the contract or by an amount used elsewhere. The national framework establishes only the absence of a federal minimum wage; practical verification requires turning to the cantonal source or, if there is no cantonal regulation, to the relevant collective agreement.
### Verification does not stop at the title
This distinction also serves to separate the rule setting any minimum level from the deductions that appear on the payslip. To follow the second step, busta paga svizzera can be consulted, while keeping verification of the cantonal regulation separate. The most useful figure for the family budget is not merely any applicable threshold, but what remains after contributions. A minimum wage, if applicable, should not be confused with net pay: AVS/AHV, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA and, when the conditions apply, LPP/BVG are deducted from the wage.
To read the payslip, the figures indicated by the source are as follows:
| Item | Data to consider | |---|---| | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% paid by the employee; 10.6% total with the employer | | AD/AC | 1.1% up to the annual ceiling | | LAINF/LAA | 0.7-1.5% depending on the sector | | LPP/BVG | coordinated salary: 7% between ages 25-34, 10% between 35-44, 15% between 45-54, 18% from age 55 until the reference age |
The percentages do not constitute a single deduction valid in every case. LPP is linked to the coordinated salary and changes by age bracket; AD/AC is indicated up to an annual ceiling, while LAINF/LAA varies according to the sector. The correct comparison therefore starts with the composition of the remuneration, not with a single rate.
LAMal/KVG also remains separate from the salary. For residents, it is compulsory health insurance, to be taken out within 3 months of arrival. Premiums are per person, vary by canton and region, and may be reduced at the cantonal level; they are neither a tax nor a salary contribution. In a cost-of-living budget, this item should not be treated as a payslip deduction.
### Two scenarios that should not be confused
If the employment relationship falls under cantonal rules, the first comparison is between the applicable rule and the remuneration provided for; only afterwards should the effect of contributions be analysed. If, on the other hand, there is no applicable cantonal minimum, the verification shifts to the relevant collective agreement, and the net calculation still follows the contribution rules applicable to the salary.
This separation also helps those who work in Switzerland and compare different offers: a figure may appear similar, but the practical result depends on the structure of contributions and separate expenses, such as LAMal. For more information on social security, consult guida AVS/LPP e rendita.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. A practical verification can follow five steps, keeping federal law, cantonal rules and the collective agreement separate.
### 1. Start at the correct level
For an employment relationship connected to the Canton of Zurich, first look for the official cantonal source describing any regulation on the minimum wage. Do not use a national figure as a substitute: at federal level there is no minimum wage. If the Canton provides for a rule, the source should guide the interpretation of its application.
### 2. Reconstruct the scope
Check the requirements, sectors concerned, monitoring procedures and competent office. These are the four points needed to understand whether the regulation concerns the relationship under review. Terms and amounts must be checked against the Canton's official source, because the cantonal framework cannot be reconstructed using a generic national rule.
### 3. Look for the contractual reference
If no applicable cantonal minimum emerges, move on to collective agreements. The question is not what the federal minimum is, because that level does not exist, but which contractual reference should be examined for the specific relationship. Do not replace the collective agreement with an amount taken from another Canton.
### 4. Separate competences and deductions
When checking remuneration, distinguish the salary rule from AVS/AHV, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA and LPP/BVG contributions. The offices also have different areas of competence: AFC/ESTV deals with IFD and VAT; UFAS/BSV concerns social security, does not set taxes; UST/BFS produces statistics, does not set rates. For the cantonal rule, it remains necessary to follow the administration and official source of the Canton.
### 5. Close the verification with the balance
Only after clarifying the rules or collective agreement, compare the remuneration with the contributions and separate expenses. LAMal/KVG, for residents, is mandatory, must be taken out within 3 months of arrival and operates with per-capita premiums: it should not be included among payroll contributions. This distinction makes the relationship between salary, social security and cost of living easier to read.

item.title: Swiss Steel announces restructuring and cuts in Germany
item.description: The Lucerne-based multinational launches a reorganization to return to profitability by 2028. Support of 17 million from the Canton for the Steeltec subsidiary.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Swiss Steel restructures its plants in Germany - Cuts have been announced, but without figures on jobs - The aim is operating profitability from 2028 - Steeltec: 17 million in support from the canton of Lucerne
## Key facts - Group and headquarters → Swiss Steel, Lucerne - Workforce → from 13'000 to 6'500 employees - Loss → 311 million euros, compared with 197 in 2024 - Volume of Swiss exports exempt from duties → reduced by 35% - Aim → operating profitability from 2028
Swiss Steel, a steel multinational headquartered in Lucerne, has announced a new restructuring following substantial losses and a significant decline in demand. The measure concerns its plants in Germany and will entail cuts in the country, CEO Frank Koch said.
In an interview published today by SonntagsZeitung, Koch did not indicate how many jobs would be eliminated. He did, however, explain that the plan aims to significantly reduce the group’s dependence on the automotive sector.
### The group's plan
The project involves reorganizing the production plants so that they can once again generate operating profits in a significantly downsized market. The next phase identified by Koch is balance-sheet recovery.
> «Our plan is to return to operating profitability from 2028».
From that point on, the group will be significantly smaller and more focused, the executive emphasized. The reorganization therefore combines production downsizing, reduced dependence on the automotive sector and a return to operating profits.
### A crisis lasting years
Swiss Steel has been facing a deep crisis for several years and has already halved its workforce, from 13'000 to 6'500 employees. Last year, the company posted a loss of 311 million euros, compared with 197 million in 2024, SonntagsZeitung reports.
The European Union’s new protectionist measures against steel imports are also weighing on the business. The volume of Swiss exports exempt from duties has been reduced by 35%. The Lucerne site is the hardest hit. Swiss Steel is in contact with the EU and the Federal Council; Koch said there are good reasons to hope for a solution.
The company left the Swiss stock exchange SIX Swiss Exchange in 2025, a decision prompted by the extensive restructurings and reorganizations of previous years. In June, the canton of Lucerne approved financial support of 17 million francs for Steeltec, a Swiss Steel subsidiary based in Emmenbrücke. The company employs 600 people, and the cantonal contribution is necessary so that the Confederation can in turn contribute an equivalent amount. ## The Swiss perspective on the restructuring
The news has a specific Swiss angle: the source separates the cuts announced in Germany from the situation at the Steeltec subsidiary in Emmenbrücke. For those who work in the sector or live in the canton of Lucerne, this distinction prevents turning the announcement into an automatic estimate of local redundancies. The number of jobs eliminated has not been disclosed, and the source does not announce cuts at Steeltec.
### Four elements not to confuse
| Area | Data in the source | Practical interpretation | |---|---|---| | Germany | Restructuring and cuts announced | The number of jobs is not indicated | | Lucerne | Site most affected by EU measures | The site is exposed to a reduction in duty-free exports | | Emmenbrücke | Steeltec employs 600 people | The support is cantonal, with a possible equivalent federal amount | | 2028 | Return to operational profitability | It is a declared objective, not a result already achieved |
The support for Steeltec has a precise structure. The canton of Lucerne has approved 17 million francs; the source specifies that this contribution is necessary for the Confederation to provide an equivalent amount. The source refers to support for Steeltec, does not describe direct payments to employees, and does not indicate any additional conditions, disbursement deadlines, or effects on individual jobs.
The second point concerns trade. The 35% reduction in the volume of Swiss duty-free exports is not presented as a measure limited to Germany: the Lucerne site is identified as the one most affected. For this reason, Swiss Steel's contacts with the European Union and the Federal Council are the channel through which developments may come, but the source does not yet communicate a solution.
The departure from SIX Swiss Exchange, which took place in 2025, should also be kept separate from the restructuring announced now. Koch linked it to the extensive restructurings and reorganizations of previous years. Those who need to navigate the job market can consult the annunci di lavoro, without using the search for new opportunities as proof of already quantified redundancies.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the dossier in Switzerland
For anyone employed, resident, or operating in the canton of Lucerne, the most prudent way to follow the matter is to start from the available data and not attribute effects to the plan that the source does not describe. Neither the number of redundancies in Germany nor an individual procedure for workers is specified. The concrete action is therefore to check updates on the site, employment, support, and timing.
### Four practical checks
1. Distinguish the location. The restructuring with cuts concerns the plants in Germany. Steeltec, on the other hand, is Swiss Steel's subsidiary based in Emmenbrücke and has 600 employees. The figure for the cuts must not automatically be applied to the Swiss subsidiary.
2. Separate the figures. The 13'000 and 6'500 employees describe the downsizing that has already taken place in the group's workforce. The 600 indicate Steeltec's staff. The 17 million francs concern cantonal support. None of these figures indicates how many new jobs will be eliminated.
3. Set the timetable. 2028 is the stated horizon for returning to operating profitability. In June, support from the canton of Lucerne was approved, while the exit from SIX Swiss Exchange dates back to 2025. The source provides no other deadlines for the cuts or for restructuring the balance sheet.
4. Follow the institutional channel. Swiss Steel is in contact with the EU and the Federal Council. At the cantonal level, the contribution to Steeltec is indicated as necessary so that the Confederation can pay an equivalent sum. The hope of a solution is reported, but its outcome has not been announced.
This sequence avoids two opposite errors: considering all 600 jobs in Emmenbrücke to be at risk or interpreting the 17 million as personal compensation. The source supports neither interpretation. Anyone who needs to assess career alternatives can look at the aziende che assumono, keeping the search for opportunities separate from the actual scale of the redundancies.

item.title: Third pillar 3a: 2026 benefits in the canton of Vaud
item.description: 2026 guide to the third pillar 3a in the canton of Vaud: tax benefits, three tax levels, indexed maximum amount and national comparison.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Three tax levels: federal, cantonal and municipal - Vaud: own cantonal law and multiplier - 3a maximum: figure indexed every year - AFC/ESTV: IFD and VAT; UFAS/BSV: social security
## Key facts - What → Swiss 3a third pillar - Focus → canton of Vaud - Taxation → direct federal tax + cantonal + municipal - Cantons → their own law and multiplier - Municipalities → multiplier applied to the cantonal tax - 3a maximum → indexed every year - AFC/ESTV → IFD and VAT - UFAS/BSV → AVS/AI/LPP, not taxes
In 2026, the Swiss 3a third pillar must be considered within three tax levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. It is the national framework of the guide and the starting point for the focus on the canton of Vaud. The tax advantage cannot be assessed as if there were a single rate valid throughout Switzerland.
### The map of responsibilities
Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier. For municipalities, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax. In Vaud, therefore, the calculation to be compared with the rest of Switzerland must separate the federal share from the cantonal and municipal components. This distinction avoids attributing a federal decision to a cantonal authority, or vice versa.
AFC/ESTV is responsible for direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations handle cantonal and municipal taxation. UFAS/BSV is responsible for social security, including AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG, but does not set taxes. UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. For anyone comparing a guida sul terzo pilastro 3a, knowing who does what is part of the verification, not an administrative detail.
The 2026 guide also considers banking and insurance providers and the contribution strategy. The comparison, however, must remain anchored to the available information: the maximum for the 3a third pillar is a figure indexed every year. It should therefore not be turned into a fixed amount unless it has been verified for the correct year. The same caution applies to other indexed figures, such as the LPP coordination threshold or deduction, the AD/AC maximum, the average LAMal/KVG premiums and the median salary.
The 3a must also be distinguished from salary deductions. AVS/AI/IPG amount to 5,3% borne by the employee and 10,6% in total with the employer; AD/AC is 1,1% up to the annual maximum. item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The EU imposes a 3 euro duty per item from third countries - Posta svizzera parcels to the EU have fallen by a double-digit percentage - Pascal Grieder expects a gradual return to normal - Grieder cites Temu's European warehouses
## Key facts - Measure → flat-rate duty of 3 euro for each item - Effective date → from July - Responsible parties → sellers or importers - Effect on Posta svizzera → double-digit decline in parcels to the EU - Company mentioned → Temu
Since July, the European Union has imposed a flat-rate duty of 3 euro for each item coming from a third country. The measure concerns small parcels and has also had repercussions for Posta svizzera: the number of parcels sent to the EU has fallen by a double-digit percentage.
The figure was reported by Pascal Grieder, director of Posta svizzera, in an interview with Schweiz am Wochenende. The executive adds that the situation should gradually return to normal. This forecast accompanies a critical assessment of the measure's objective: Grieder doubts that protecting the market from Chinese imports will actually be achieved.
### The rule and the consequences indicated
The duty is flat-rate: the source indicates the same unit amount, 3 euro, for each item coming from a third country. In principle, payment is the responsibility of the seller or importer. Some merchants, however, pass this amount on to consumers. The rule therefore identifies a main responsible party, while the cost may reach whoever makes the purchase.
Grieder's point concerns the organization of shipments. The executive cites Temu, a low-cost Chinese online sales site, and reports that companies like this are opening large warehouses in Europe. Parcels are shipped from those warehouses and, according to his assessment, thus avoid paying the fee. For Grieder, this step calls into question the practical effectiveness of the duty in relation to the stated objective of protecting the market from Chinese imports.
The connection with Switzerland emerges from the data on Posta svizzera's volumes: the European measure is described not only as a rule for sellers and importers, but also as a change that has already had repercussions on Posta svizzera shipments to the EU. The director indicates a decline expressed as a double-digit percentage and expects a gradual recovery. The news thus brings together a new European duty, a different organization of shipments, and a response observed in Swiss postal activity. ## How to read the impact
To understand the practical effect of the duty, it is necessary to keep distinct the origin of the item, the party required to pay, and the price ultimately borne by the consumer. The source does not present these three elements as equivalent: the measure indicates the amount per item coming from a third country; the seller or importer is responsible in principle; some merchants may pass on the cost. For anyone observing a final price, this distinction avoids confusing the party responsible for payment with the one who ultimately bears the amount.
### Three elements to keep separate
| Situation indicated | Rule or figure | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Item from a third country | 3 euros per item | The reference is the individual item | | Responsibility for payment | Seller or importer | The cost may be passed on to the consumer | | Shipment from a European warehouse | Temu avoids the tax according to Grieder | The indicated route changes the outcome | | Postal packages to the EU | Double-digit decline | Grieder expects a gradual return to normal |
The first element to consider is therefore the unit to which the source links the duty: the item. The measure is flat-rate and refers to each item coming from a third country. This wording helps interpret the rule without turning it into a calculation based on the total price of the package.
The second element is the allocation of the burden. Responsibility in principle remains with the seller or importer; the consumer may, however, bear the cost when the merchant passes it on. For those comparing offers, the point to verify is whether the merchant passes on the amount, without confusing the responsible party with the party that actually pays.
The third element is logistics. Grieder uses Temu to show that opening large warehouses in Europe may make it possible to ship from there while avoiding the tax. ## Key facts - LPP/BVG on coordinated salary → 7% (25-34), 10% (35-44), 15% (45-54), 18% (55+ until reference age) - AHV/IV/EO → 5.3% employee; 10.6% total with employer - ALV/AC → 1.1% up to the annual ceiling - UVG/LAA → 0.7%-1.5% depending on the sector - KVG/LAMal → mandatory for residents, to be taken out within 3 months of arrival
The LPP/BVG rates on the coordinated salary are the starting point of the 2026 guide: 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, and 18% from 55 until the reference age. The territorial focus is the canton of Lucerne, while the comparison remains national. The topics include contributions, withdrawal, buy-back of gaps, and pension planning.
### Contribution table
| Age group | LPP/BVG on coordinated salary | |---|---| | 25-34 | 7% | | 35-44 | 10% | | 45-54 | 15% | | 55+ until reference age | 18% |
These percentages refer to the coordinated salary and should not be confused with other deductions or an insurance premium. On the payslip, AHV/IV/EO amounts to 5.3% for the employee, with a total of 10.6% including the employer. ALV/AC is indicated at 1.1% up to the annual ceiling, while UVG/LAA varies from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. Correct interpretation therefore starts from the item and the base to which it applies, not just the percentage.
The distinction also matters for institutional competence. FSIO/BSV is the reference for social security — AHV, IV, and LPP/BVG — and does not set taxes. FTA/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT. Cantonal administrations follow cantonal and municipal taxes; each canton has its own law and multiplier, while the municipality applies the multiplier to the cantonal one. FSO/BFS provides statistics and does not set rates.
Data indexed annually includes the LPP/BVG threshold and coordination deduction, the ALV/AC ceiling, the third pillar 3a maximum, average KVG/LAMal premiums, and the median salary. To connect basic and occupational pensions, the reader can use the 'AVS/LPP and pension' guide (), keeping the updatable values separate from the percentages indicated by age group. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical reading starts from three distinct levels: coordinated salary, salary contributions and insurance premiums. The LPP scale is not a percentage to be applied indiscriminately to every figure on the payslip: it concerns the coordinated salary. When entering a new age bracket, the reference percentage changes. The comparison remains clear only if the calculation base is kept separate.
### From the percentage to the payslip
The first check concerns pension and social security items. AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC and LAINF/LAA have different rates and bases: the first item shows 5.3% charged to the employee and 10.6% overall with the employer, AD/AC is linked to the annual maximum and LAINF/LAA depends on the sector. The second check concerns LAMal/KVG. It is mandatory for residents, must be taken out within 3 months of arrival, provides for per-capita premiums and is neither a tax nor a salary contribution. Premiums vary by canton or region, and premium reductions are cantonal. To check the items without adding them incorrectly, it is advisable to start from busta paga svizzera.
### Lucerne and the three tax levels
The third level concerns taxation. In Switzerland, there are direct federal tax, cantonal taxes and municipal taxes. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier; municipalities apply the multiplier to the cantonal tax. This keeps pension planning distinct from tax analysis, even when both affect the available budget. AFC/ESTV is associated with direct federal tax and VAT, while cantonal administrations manage the cantonal and municipal levels. UFAS/BSV does not set tax rates, and UST/BFS does not establish them through statistics.
In the canton of Lucerne, the territorial focus should therefore be considered alongside the national comparison: LPP percentages are structured by age brackets for the coordinated salary, while various economic and insurance data are subject to annual updates. The maximum for the 3a third pillar is also indexed; to compare it with LPP, use terzo pilastro 3a only after verifying the official values.

3. Separate the salary items from health coverage. AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA and LPP belong in the analysis of contributions; LAMal has per-capita premiums, is not a salary contribution, and residents must take it out within 3 months of arrival.

item.title: Swiss LPP second pillar: 2026 guide for Geneva
item.description: Practical guide to the 2026 LPP second pillar: contributions, buy-ins to cover gaps and pension planning in the canton of Geneva and at the national level.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The second LPP pillar supplements the AVS/AI pension. - Contributions vary according to the worker's age brackets. - Buying back contribution gaps makes it possible to optimize taxation. - LPP legislation is regulated at federal level by the UFAS.
## Key facts - Contribution age 25-34: 7% - Contribution age 35-44: 10% - Contribution age 45-54: 15% - Contribution age 55+ years: 18% - Pension authority: UFAS/BSV
The Swiss pension system is structured around three pillars, with the second, known as LPP (Occupational Pension Act), playing a central role in maintaining one's standard of living after retirement. At national level, this pillar is financed through equal contributions paid by the employee and the employer, calculated on the coordinated salary. The Federal Social Insurance Office (UFAS/BSV) defines the guidelines that pension funds must follow, ensuring uniformity throughout Switzerland, including the canton of Geneva.
### Contribution mechanism The LPP contribution structure follows a progression based on the worker's age. For the 25-34 age bracket, the rate is 7%; for ages 35-44 it rises to 10%; for ages 45-54 it reaches 15%; while for workers aged 55 through the reference age, the contribution is set at 18%. These payments, which also include a portion for disability and death risks, are accumulated in a personal account with the pension institution selected by the employer. It is essential to understand that, although the rates are uniform at federal level, the operational management and the range of supplementary pension plans may vary among the different insurance institutions operating in the canton. For those working in Geneva, as throughout the Confederation, the employer has a legal obligation to affiliate its employees with an authorized pension fund. Transparency in communication between the pension institution and the insured person is guaranteed by federal legislation, which requires the annual dispatch of the pension certificate, a fundamental document for monitoring the development of one's capital and planning one's financial future with awareness, bearing in mind that any contribution gap will directly affect the amount of the future pension. The analysis of occupational pension provision requires particular attention to the buyback of contribution gaps, an operation that makes it possible to increase the capital saved and, at the same time, reduce the taxable base in the canton of residence or employment. In Geneva, as in other cantons, amounts paid to fill LPP gaps are deductible from taxable income, making this strategy particularly effective for optimizing the overall tax burden. However, it is necessary to verify that the regulations of one’s pension fund permit such payments and that there are no restrictions related to early withdrawals previously made for the purchase of residential property.
### Planning strategies Proper pension planning involves constantly monitoring one’s pension certificate. In the event of a change of employment, the worker must transfer their retirement assets to the new pension fund. If the new employer does not offer an LPP solution, the entire capital must be paid into a vested benefits account or policy with a bank or insurance institution. This procedure is strictly regulated by federal law to prevent capital from being dispersed.
Another relevant aspect concerns early withdrawal for the purchase of a primary residence. Swiss law permits part of the LPP capital to be used as collateral or for direct financing, but this operation reduces future pension benefits and coverage in the event of disability or death. The decision to make a buyback or an early withdrawal must be assessed with the utmost care, preferably with the support of expert advisers who are familiar with the specific features of the Geneva tax system and the federal rules in force. The stability of the LPP system is guaranteed by the constant supervision of the competent authorities, which ensure that pension institutions comply with the solvency requirements necessary to meet the commitments undertaken toward insured persons, thereby guaranteeing the security of long-term savings nationwide.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. To manage one’s position in the second pillar effectively, it is necessary to follow a structured procedure that begins with the periodic analysis of the documentation sent by one’s pension fund. Every year, the insured person receives a statement indicating the accumulated capital, the benefits in the event of death or disability and, above all, the maximum amount available for buy-in to cover any pension gaps. Keeping these documents properly archived is the first step toward informed management, as they form the basis for every future financial decision.
### Operating procedure Anyone wishing to make a buy-in must first request the official calculation of the deductible amount from their pension fund. Once the document has been obtained, it will be possible to make the payment by bank transfer, ensuring that the receipt is kept for the tax return. It is essential to remember that tax deductions are linked to the canton of tax domicile: for those working in Geneva, the relevant legal framework is the cantonal legislation that incorporates the federal provisions on the deductibility of pension contributions.
For those wishing to examine their income situation and the tax impact of LPP contributions in greater depth, or who need a broader overview of their payslip in relation to social obligations, the site provides specific calculation tools. Using calcolatore stipendio makes it possible to clearly visualize the impact of social deductions on gross salary, facilitating understanding of the available net amount. In addition, for those planning their pension future or assessing how to optimize their tax burden, consulting the guides on dichiarazione delle imposte is a mandatory step to avoid formal errors that could compromise the tax benefits obtainable through payments into the second pillar. Planning for tomorrow starts today, through careful and informed management of one’s pension rights and obligations in the Swiss context.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The 60th assembly was held in Melide - SwissAccounting Svizzera Italiana has 847 members - Four candidates obtained the federal diploma - Forty-eight passed the examination for the certificate
## Key facts - Event → 60th Ordinary General Assembly - Location → Swiss Diamond Boutique Hotel La Romantica in Melide - Members → 847 - Federal diploma → 4 candidates - Federal certificate → 48 candidates - Date of the change → October 1, 2026 - First designation → «Professional Master» - Second designation → «Professional Bachelor»
### The ceremony in Melide
Melide hosted the 60th Ordinary General Assembly of SwissAccounting Svizzera Italiana, held at the Swiss Diamond Boutique Hotel La Romantica. The association currently has 847 members. The meeting addressed the main assembly topics and, at the opening, provided space for the awarding of the new graduates from the 2026 examination session.
Four candidates obtained the Federal Diploma as Experts in Finance and Controlling. The best average was achieved by Moro Ludovico, with a prize offered by Progel SA - Manno. The same group includes Bosisio Nicolò, Butti Fiorella Cristina, and Ferraro Giuseppe.
Meanwhile, 48 candidates passed the examination for the Federal Certificate as Specialists in Finance and Accounting. The three best averages were achieved by Ana Maria Stan, Federico Vernavà, and Francesca Carrara, who were awarded by BancaStato. The association's communication also lists the other candidates who obtained the certificate.
The Committee also informed those present about the amendment to the Federal Vocational and Professional Education and Training Act, effective from October 1, 2026. Those holding the Federal Diploma as Experts in Finance and Controlling may add the designation «Professional Master». Those holding the Federal Certificate as Specialists in Finance and Accounting may instead use «Professional Bachelor».
During the assembly, the activities carried out by the individual members of the Committee during the last financial year were presented. The Assembly reconfirmed the outgoing Committee: Kevin Kaufmann as president, Ines Guarisco as vice-president, and Vincenza Bianchi, Sergio Bizzozero, Fabiano Bonardi, Alessandro Gottardi, and Fabrizio Ruscitti as members. The SwissAccounting Svizzera Italiana School offers its courses in Lugano-Trevano. ## The meaning of the two designations
The change communicated during the assembly concerns how holders of the two pathways can add a designation alongside their qualification. The text presents a distinct correspondence, which it is best to preserve without conflating the qualifications.
### The correspondence indicated
| Qualification held | Associated designation as of 1° ottobre 2026 | |---|---| | Federal Diploma of Expert in Finance and Controlling | «Professional Master» | | Federal Certificate of Specialist in Finance and Accounting | «Professional Bachelor» |
The term used in the communication is to add alongside. The two expressions are therefore presented as designations to be added to the qualification held, with a different formula for each qualification. The practical reading starts here: the Federal Diploma should not be associated with the designation intended for the Federal Certificate, and vice versa.
The source cites two different time references. The 2026 examination session is the one for the newly graduated students honored in Melide; 1° ottobre 2026, on the other hand, is the date indicated for the amendment to the Federal Law on Vocational Education and Training. Separating these two elements helps to read the news correctly: one concerns the examination session, the other the use of the new designations.
The presence of a federal law links the association's communication to a vocational education and training topic that is not limited to the ceremony in Melide. The source, however, restricts the information to the possibility of using the two formulas and does not describe any further administrative steps or other effects. For this reason, the central point remains the title-designation pair.
Those considering a pathway in finance and accounting can use this distinction to accurately interpret the qualifications mentioned by the Scuola SwissAccounting Svizzera Italiana, which offers its courses in Lugano-Trevano. To complement training with the search for professional opportunities, the annunci di lavoro are also available.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to correctly apply the new provision
### Four practical checks
1. Start from the qualification actually held. The first check concerns the designation: Federal Diploma of Expert in Finance and Controlling or Federal Certificate of Specialist in Finance and Accounting.
2. Link the qualification to the corresponding designation. The Federal Diploma is paired with «Professional Master». The Federal Certificate is paired with «Professional Bachelor».
3. Keep in mind the date indicated by the Committee. The amendment to the Federal Act on Vocational and Professional Education and Training concerns 1° ottobre 2026. This date must be distinguished from the 2026 examination session mentioned for the award ceremony for recent graduates.
4. Reproduce the designations without reversing them. The assembly's communication associates each designation with a single qualification among those indicated. The final check therefore consists of comparing your qualification with the correspondence given by the source.
This is the operational scope of the news item. The source does not indicate forms, applications or other documents to submit in order to use the designations; instead, it provides the relationship between the two qualifications and the two designations, together with the date of the change. For those pursuing training in the field, the only training path mentioned is that of the Scuola SwissAccounting Svizzera Italiana, with courses offered in Lugano-Trevano.
The professional aspect can be explored separately by consulting the aziende che assumono, without confusing the designation linked to the qualification with the Certificate or Diploma itself. The distinction remains the essential step for correctly presenting the indicated qualification.

item.description: Micasa will part with four stores by January 2027: Crissier will close by the end of 2026. Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs involved; no comment on jobs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Micasa will part with four stores by January 2027 - Crissier will close by the end of 2026 - Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs involved - The network had 30 branches last year
## Key facts - Business → furniture and decoration - Exit from the Migros group → 2025 - Network acquired → 30 branches - Locations involved → Crissier, Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs - Crissier deadline → end of 2026 - Overall deadline → by January 2027 - Reported ownership → group of Swiss investors - Stated reason → economic situation and market conditions
Last year, Micasa's 30 branches, four of them in French-speaking Switzerland, were taken over by the managers of the former subsidiary. The transaction came after the brand left the orbit of the Migros group in 2025. Now the network is being scaled back: the economic news site Inside Paradeplatz revealed that Micasa will part with four stores by January 2027.
### Four locations involved
The Crissier store, in the canton of Vaud, will close by the end of 2026. The other three sites listed are Langendorf (SO), Brügg (BE) and Buchs (SG). The news therefore concerns locations spread across several cantons, while the Crissier store is the one for which the source already indicates a precise deadline.
The figure of 30 branches makes it possible to gauge the scope of the announcement without confusing it with a complete exit from the market. The source refers to four stores that Micasa will part with, while it does not describe the closure of all the branches.
The sequence described by the source is not limited to a reduction in outlets. The ownership issue is also being reopened. The results of the management entrusted to the executives of the former subsidiary reportedly did not meet expectations. The company was therefore reportedly taken over urgently by a group of Swiss investors. The names of the investors have not been disclosed.
Micasa operates in the mid-range segment of furniture and decoration. The brand attributes the difficulties to the current economic situation and the changing market conditions. This is the reason given by the company, not an additional assessment of individual stores or individual cantons.
The employment issue remains open. At the time of publication, no comment had been released on any possible job cuts. Therefore, the source makes it possible to establish locations, timelines and ownership changes, but not to quantify the consequences for staff. The position of the workers remains separate from that of the customers. The company has not commented on possible job cuts; this does not allow us to infer either a number of redundancies or a guarantee that jobs will be maintained. item.title: Gotthard: data analysis to avoid queues
item.description: Fabrizio Bacchini created the Gottardo Live app by analyzing 19 thousand FEDRO reports. Find out how to monitor traffic and better plan your trip.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Bacchini analyzes the traffic of the Gotthard every day. - From 11 July, traffic jams on 82 out of 83 days. - On July 18, the queue reached 20 kilometers. - The Gottardo Live app uses official data.
## Key Facts - Who is frequency → Fabrizio Bacchini, a 57-year-old manager from Zug; four-five monthly crossings - Data analyzed → about 19 thousand reports since the beginning of July - Peak → 20 kilometers of queue and 200 minutes of waiting on July 18 - Critical → from 11 am to 6 pm - App and threshold → Gotthard Live, free of charge; 10-20 minutes of traffic jam acceptable
### Monitoring built on data
In the text of 2 October 2026, Fabrizio Bacchini's story tells how an everyday mobility problem became a digital project. The 57-year-old manager from Zug crosses the Gotthard tunnel four to five times a month for work. To decide when to leave, he checks traffic data every day and looks for the moment when the queue starts to shrink.
Since the beginning of July, it has sifted through about 19 thousand official reports. Its system records waiting times, expressed in minutes, and the length of queues, indicated in kilometers, for both directions of travel every five minutes. The basis is the communications of the Federal Roads Office, FEDRO. Official warnings on accidents, road closures and traffic flow regulations are also included in the monitoring.
The result returns the frequency of the problem. Since 11 July, traffic jams have been recorded in front of the tunnel on 82 out of 83 days. The peak came on Saturday 18 July, with 20 kilometres of queues southbound and waiting times of up to 200 minutes. In September, outside of holiday periods, traffic jams formed every weekday.
The slot between 11 and 18 is practically always congested. Bacchini, on the other hand, indicates early morning and late afternoon as the times that usually offer the best conditions. However, the choice also depends on the day of the week: looking at the map, it follows the moment when the queue begins to shorten.
Passion led to the birth of Gottardo Live, a free app that uses official data and signals when the traffic jam forms, lengthens or begins to dissolve. Bacchini says he programmed it to retrieve information every five minutes, then checking it with webcams and the real situation. At the beginning, he dedicated up to five hours a day to the project. Today the system is more stable, but continues to check the data daily. ## What changes for those who have to go through the tunnel
For those who live or work in Switzerland and have to travel the southern axis, the material collected by Bacchini offers a practical reading: traffic should not be considered only as an event related to holidays. The observed series, on the other hand, shows a recurring presence, with a central band of the day almost always difficult and with differences related to the weekly calendar.
### From photography to decision
The useful distinction is between the historical data and the real-time situation. Comparisons between individual days serve to recognize patterns: when the traffic jam tends to form, when it reaches its longest phase and when it begins to dissolve. The app notification follows precisely these phases. For those who have to organize a crossing, the most informative moment is not necessarily the one when the queue is already at its maximum, but the one when the map shows a change. This is the logic that Bacchini applies when he observes the beginning of the reduction of the column.
The time slot indicated by his analysis can be read as a grid, not as a promise. Between 11 and 18 congestion is described as practically constant; early morning and late afternoon are the windows that are usually better. The day of the week remains an autonomous variable. The fact that in September traffic jams occurred every weekday prevents the problem from being reduced to only large exoduses.
The comparison with the previous situation is also concrete. Bacchini explains that an app already existed, but it was full of advertising and forced people to search within it for traffic information. Gottardo Live was created to directly use official data and report the evolution of the queue. This makes the reading described in the story more immediate, without turning the app into a rule that is the same for every motorist.
The limit of ten or twenty minutes is Bacchini's personal one: beyond that threshold, he prefers to take the pace. It is not a threshold attributed to the road network nor a general recommendation. It is an example of how a measured figure can become an individual choice.
For those who want to combine the reading of traffic with a comparison with mezzi pubblici, however, this is another evaluation plan. The same goes for the costo della vita in Svizzera: history does not offer figures on this aspect, so it is not possible to derive an economic cost from the kilometers of queue.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to use analytics before you go
The story allows you to derive an operational sequence based only on the available information. There is no need to transform the app into a fixed calendar: the method consists of verifying the update, reading the queue phase and comparing the data with the observed patterns.
### Four essential steps
1. Open Gotthard Live and start with the official data. The app is free of charge and uses FEDRO reports. The reference must be the current situation, because the system collects data every five minutes.
2. Check both directions of travel. The information considered by Bacchini includes waiting times in minutes and queue length in kilometers. Before deciding, it is therefore necessary to distinguish the south direction from the opposite one, without automatically transferring data to the other direction.
3. Read the movement of the queue. The signal does not only concern the presence of the traffic jam: it indicates whether it is forming, if it is lengthening or if it is beginning to dissolve. Push notifications must be interpreted with the same care with which Bacchini has adjusted their frequency, avoiding an arrival too early or too close.
4. Compare the update with the day and time. His analysis identifies recurrences, but leaves room for checking the moment. Early morning and late afternoon are the references indicated as generally best; the time slot between 11 and 18 is the one described as congested. If the wait exceeds the personal threshold, Bacchini's criterion is to take the pace.
This procedure serves to distinguish official data, their evolution and individual decision. For those who cross the tunnel for work, it concerns first of all the time of the journey; the other economic aspects remain separate from the traffic analysis.
The project shows how much work there is behind a seemingly simple notice: scheduling data recovery, comparing it with webcams, checking the real situation and adjusting notifications. Those who use the app can limit themselves to the final result, while the daily check remains the step that makes the update readable. item.description: Novartis obtains the worldwide license on ABO2203 from Abogen: 575 million initial dollars and potential payments up to about 7.2 billion.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Novartis obtains worldwide license on ABO2203. - Abogen receives an initial $575 million. - The agreement can reach about 7.2 billion. - ABO2203 mRNA is used against B lymphocytes.
## Key Facts - Active ingredient: ABO2203 - License: Worldwide Exclusive - Initial payment: $575 million - Value: CHF 480 million - Potential: up to approximately $7.2 billion - Technology: mRNA - Development: clinical phase
### The structure of the agreement Novartis expands its portfolio of RNA-based therapeutics thanks to a license agreement with Abogen Biosciences, a Chinese biotech company. The agreement was communicated by Abogen itself in a note.
At the heart is ABO2203, a new active ingredient for the treatment of autoimmune diseases. The agreement gives Novartis an exclusive worldwide license on the active ingredient and provides options on additional drug programs based on Abogen's RNA platform.
The expected initial payment for Abogen is $575 million, or CHF 480 million. The potential portion of the transaction can be as high as $7.2 billion if all options on the other programs are exercised and the respective development, approval and commercialization milestones are met.
Abogen will also be entitled to possible licensing revenue on future sales of the products. The structure therefore combines an initial component, a part related to milestones and a possible return on sales.
### How does ABO2203 ABO2203 uses mRNA, the messenger ribonucleic acid, to induce the body to produce a molecule on its own that attacks and eliminates B lymphocytes in a targeted manner. These cells play an important role in many autoimmune diseases. According to Abogen, the drug is already in clinical development.
RNA technology had made a lot of headlines especially thanks to the Covid vaccines from Moderna and Biontech. However, it has existed for several decades and had previously been tested mainly in cancer research. The press release thus puts in the same agreement an active ingredient already in clinical development and a platform from which other programs can derive. ## What does potential value mean
To read the agreement from an economic point of view, it is necessary to keep separate the initial payment, the conditions for subsequent payments and the possible revenues related to sales. The figure of about 7.2 billion is not presented as an initial outlay: the source links it to the exercise of all options and the achievement of the expected goals.
### The components of the agreement
| Voice | Practical reading | |---|---| | Initial payment | USD 575 million, with an indicated value of CHF 480 million. | | Options | Additional programs based on Abogen's RNA platform. | | Milestones | Development, approval and commercialisation of the programmes concerned. | | Future Sales | Possible licensing revenue for Abogen. |
The correct comparison is therefore not between two sums available at the same time. The $575 million is reported as the initial payment; instead, the maximum value depends on a sequence of conditions. All options for the other programs must be exercised first, then the respective development, approval, and commercialization milestones must be met.
For a reader in Switzerland, the reference to 480 million francs makes the scale of the initial component immediate, while the total potential remains expressed in dollars. The currency, however, does not change the structure of the agreement: the first amount and the maximum potential belong to different times and conditions.
The scientific profile must also be read separately from the commercial one. ABO2203 is described as already in clinical development, but the agreement also links additional payments to approval and marketing. The text therefore distinguishes the development of the drug from the steps necessary to get to sales.
For the daily life of residents, the concrete connection remains informative: the source describes a transaction between companies, not a payment intended for families. ### Five operational steps
1. **Identify the object.** The first reference is ABO2203, an active ingredient intended for the treatment of autoimmune diseases. This avoids confusing it with the broader RNA-based platform.
2. Separate license and options. The license granted to Novartis is exclusive and worldwide for ABO2203. The options instead cover additional drug programs based on Abogen's RNA platform.
3. Record the amount and currency. The initial payment should be recorded as 575 million dollars, with the indicated equivalent of 480 million francs. The two figures describe the same initial payment, not two separate payments.
4. Rebuild the condition for the maximum. The value of up to about $7.2 billion requires the exercise of all options and the achievement of development, approval and commercialization goals. The figure should therefore be read as a scenario subject to these steps.
5. Keep future sales separate. Abogen may have possible license revenue on future product sales. This item should not be confused with either the initial payment or the milestones listed above.

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. To build a comparison that can be used in 2026, it is advisable to proceed by separating salary data, contributions and related costs. The sequence avoids confusing national statistics with a cantonal rule or private expenditure.
### Five-Step Procedure
1. Define the perimeter. Indicate profession, sector, canton Bern and year 2026. When the official data available is the median salary, use that and do not mix different years, professions or sectors.
2. Check the applicable minimum wage. There is no single threshold at federal level; some cantons have their own. The comparison must therefore distinguish the national framework from the rule of the canton in question.
3. Separate the salary items. Consider AHV/IV/EO at 5.3% for the employee and 10.6% overall with the employer, ALV/HC at 1.1% up to the annual ceiling and UVG/LAA between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. For BVG, check the coordinated salary and age range: 7%, 10%, 15% or 18%.
4. Keep taxation separate. Direct federal tax and VAT are part of the FTA/ESTV; the cantonal and municipal parts are the responsibility of the cantonal administrations. The FSO/BFS provides statistics, while the FSIO/BSV concerns social security and not tax rates.
5. Add expenses that are not wage contributions. The KVG is mandatory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival. Premiums depend on the canton and region, premium reductions are cantonal and adult deductibles follow the options provided. Do not include this insurance in taxes or salary contributions.
The final sheet should report separately the salary data, working conditions and related exits. In addition to the maximum working hours of 45 or 50 hours, it records the minimum holidays, equal to four weeks or five under 20 years of age. Maternity and paternity follow separate rules: 14 weeks at 80% for maternity and two weeks for paternity.
To get a consistent salary estimate after these checks, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Opening a business in the Canton of Graubünden: register and costs
item.description: In the canton of Graubünden, the course combines legal form, commercial register, minimum capital, registration fees and insurance obligations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Legal form, register and minimum capital are the first issues. - The Swiss tax authorities operate on three levels. - FTA/ESTV follows IFD and VAT; the cantons the local levy. - AHV/IV/EO, ALV/CA, UVG and BVG have an impact on wages.
## Key Facts - Taxation → federal IFD, cantonal and municipal taxes - Municipal multiplier → applied to the cantonal tax - FTA/ESTV → IFD and VAT - AHV/IV/EO → 5.3% employee; 10.6% overall - AD/AC → 1.1% up to the annual ceiling - UVG/LAA → 0.7%-1.5% depending on the sector - KVG → mandatory for residents - Maximum hours → 45 or 50 hours per week
### The perimeter of the start Opening a business in the canton of Graubünden requires keeping the corporate project and the cost of management separate. The choice of legal form, registration in the commercial register, minimum capital, registration fees and insurance obligations belong to the same path, but they are not the same item. An orderly estimate must therefore distinguish what is needed to start the business from what is used with taxation and wages.
The first reference is the tax system. In Switzerland, the levy has three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier on the cantonal tax. In Graubünden, this distinction prevents a single multiplier from being read as if it represented the entire tax account.
Administrative responsibilities must also be divided. The FTA/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT. The cantonal administrations manage the cantonal and municipal components. The FSIO/BSV covers social security, including AHV/IV and BVG, but does not set taxes. The FSO/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. For a new job, confusing these roles can lead to putting the correct entry in front of the wrong office.
The practical point is to separate the opening cost from the operating cost. The registration fees belong to the start-up; taxation, on the other hand, follows the three levels provided, while insurance obligations can be linked to salaries or, for the KVG, to residence. To prepare the dichiarazione delle imposte, it is advisable to keep the entries in the register, tax and insurance separate from the start. ## From the register to recurring costs
### When the business takes on The registration fee is a start-up item; the cost of labour, on the other hand, follows each salary. If the business in Graubünden has employees, the bill must be calculated on the contributions indicated from the source, without confusing them with taxes. The AHV/IV/EO is 5.3% borne by the employee and 10.6% overall by the employer. The ALV/HC is 1.1% up to the annual ceiling. The UVG/LAA varies from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. For BVG/BVG, the rates on the coordinated salary are 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54 and 18% from 55 years of age up to the reference age.
| Item | Parameter to be budgeted | | AHV/IV/EO | 5.3% employee; 10.6% overall | | AD/AC | 1.1% up to the annual ceiling | | UVG/LAA | 0.7%-1.5% depending on the sector | | BVG/BVG | 7%, 10%, 15% or 18% depending on age |
The table is used to distinguish between a payroll charge and a tax. In addition, the ALV/AC ceiling should not be converted into a fixed figure if it is not checked for the reference year. The indexed figures change every year; the same caution applies to the BVG coordination threshold and deduction, the average KVG premiums and the median salary.
The KVG/KVG follows another criterion. For those residing in Switzerland, it is mandatory and must be taken out within three months of arrival. It is a private insurance with per capita premiums, not a tax or a salary contribution. Premiums change by canton and region, while premium reduction is cantonal. In the family budget, therefore, the cost of living and the paycheck must be read on separate levels: the health premium is not calculated as a percentage of salary. To learn more about this step, you can use the confronto LAMal/cassa malati.
If the business takes over, the working rules also apply. There is no federal minimum wage, although some cantons have their own. The maximum working time is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and sales, or 50 hours in other sectors. The minimum holidays are four weeks, five under the age of 20; maternity leave lasts 14 weeks at 80% through EO and paternity leave two weeks. The notice periods are one month in the first year, two from the second to the ninth and three from the tenth.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Practical procedure in the canton of Graubünden
### Five Steps to Order Quote 1. Define the legal form. To build the estimate, associate the chosen form with the minimum capital provided for by the course and keep this item separate from the registration fees. 2. Isolate start-up costs. Record commercial register fees as a separate entry and do not merge them with future taxes or payroll contributions. The distinction makes it possible to understand which disbursements belong to the opening and which to the management. 3. Separate tax competences. For direct federal tax and VAT, the reference is the FTA/ESTV; for the cantonal and municipal part, the cantonal administrations are responsible. The municipal multiplier should be read as applied to the cantonal tax, within a three-tier system. 4. Prepare the work block. If there are salaries, set up the calculation with AHV/IV/EO, ALV/CA, UVG/LAA and BVP/BVG. Use the annual ceiling of the ALV/HC, the sector for the UVG/LAA and the salary coordinated with the age group for the BVG, without replacing these parameters with outdated amounts. 5. Check residence and staff rules. For residents, the KVG must be concluded within three months of arrival; premiums and reductions depend on the canton and region. If you are hiring, plan schedules, holidays, maternity, paternity and notice periods according to the indicated limits.
The check does not end with registration. The figures indexed each year include the 3rd pillar 3a ceiling, the BVG coordination threshold and deduction, the AD/AC ceiling, the average KVG premiums and the median salary. For this reason, a quote built with a fixed figure risks quickly becoming outdated: the parameters must be updated on the official source before using them.
### A readable file The clearest sequence is therefore the legal form and capital, register and start-up fees, taxation, salaries and insurance, then an annual review of the indexed values. In this way, the start-up can distinguish the registration price from the recurring labour costs and the health coverage of the residents, without attributing to the FSIO/BSV or the FSO/BFS tax responsibilities that the source does not assign to them.
To turn the salary portion of the estimate into an operational estimate, use the calcolatore stipendio.
